question.prompt: Alice, Bob, and Charlie were on a hike and were wondering how far away the nearest town was. When Alice said, “We are at least \(6\) miles away,” Bob replied, “We are at most \(5\) miles away.” Charlie then remarked, “Actually the nearest town is at most \(4\) miles away.” It turned out that none of the three statements was true. Let \(d\) be the distance in miles to the nearest town. Which of the following intervals is the set of all possible values of \(d?\)

solutions.title: Turn false statements into bounds
solutions.explanation:
Since every statement is false, negate each person's bound, including its equality case. Alice's false claim gives \(d<6\). Bob's gives \(d>5\), and Charlie's gives \(d>4\).

The condition \(d>5\) already ensures \(d>4\), so all three conditions together reduce to
\[
5<d<6.
\]
Every distance in this range makes all three statements false. Therefore the set of possible distances is \(\boxed{(5,6)}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
